prediction_ref.short_label: Frontier-lab governance frameworks converge on shared quantitative-harm thresholds by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Today's own prediction lands directly on Friday's OpenAI publication of the Frontier Governance Framework. The document maps OpenAI's existing Preparedness Framework onto disclosure obligations under California's Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act (SB 53, in force from January 1) and the EU AI Act's Code of Practice for General Purpose AI, covering risk assessment and mitigation across cyber offense, CBRN, harmful manipulation, and loss of control plus model reporting, security risk management, incident response, and external expert input — and notably anchors systemic risk to specific quantitative thresholds: scenarios where a model contributes to greater than 50 fatalities or causes $1 billion in property damages from a single incident. This is the first time a frontier lab has tied its public governance document to numeric SB 53 annual-update triggers, making the language no longer a vague qualitative posture but a regulator-facing numeric anchor that California AG staff drafting SB 53 implementation guidance, EU AI Office reviewers scoring CoP signatories, and enterprise procurement teams writing model-risk clauses will benchmark every Tier-1 lab against. The Anthropic Series H + Opus 4.8 GA across Bedrock, Vertex, and Microsoft 365 Copilot the same Friday underscores how quickly other Tier-1 labs are scaling against public-company-grade governance scrutiny, leaving Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI, and Mistral with a forcing function rather than an optional posture.
